content:
**Visual observations from test image:**
- Soybean plant with dead/brown dried lower leaves showing severe necrosis
- Upper portion still has green leaves — disease progressing from bottom up
- Dead leaflets appear to have dropped/are dying while petioles remain attached to stem
- Field background shows mature/late-season crop

**Analysis:**
The key feature is dead lower leaflets with petioles remaining attached to the stem — this is the hallmark of **Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS)**. The SDS description states "leaflets eventually drop but petioles remain on the stem" and symptoms progress from the lower canopy upward. The pattern of dead lower tissue contrasting with still-green upper leaves matches SDS at late growth stages.

The reference SDS collage confirms: field patches of affected plants with interveinal chlorosis/necrosis progressing to death from lower canopy up.
